title_tag: 10 Best Family Resorts in Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Dubai family resorts from €76 to €471 a night compared on kids' clubs, included waterpark days, theme-park tickets, family rooms and extra-bed costs.
h1_main: 10 Best Family Resorts and Hotels in Dubai in 2026
author_role: 10 Dubai family resorts compared on nightly price, kids' club, waterpark or theme-park access, family rooms and extra-bed rules
lead: For most families the Dubai resort to book is Atlantis, The Palm at €381 a night: daily Aquaventure World and Lost World Aquarium access is included, with a supervised kids' club and 16 restaurants. The value waterpark pick is Le Meridien Mina Seyahi at €235 (unlimited Jungle Bay waterpark, kids' club, 1,200 m beach), Lapita at €235 puts theme-park access in the room rate a short walk from LEGOLAND and MOTIONGATE, and Rove At The Park at €76 is the cheapest bed next to the parks.

The catch most families miss: every price here is for two adults, and four of the ten have no extra beds at all; the rest charge AED 100–200 per extra bed per night. All 10 were compared on price for the same night, kids' club, waterpark or theme-park access, family room size, child and extra-bed rules, and beach. Filter by waterpark, beach, theme parks, kids' club or budget below, or jump to the comparison table.

review: Atlantis, The Palm is the resort we would book for a first family trip to Dubai. The €381 a night Ocean King Room includes something no other hotel on this page matches: free daily entry to Aquaventure World, the waterpark with the Tower of Neptune and Tower of Poseidon slides, and to the Lost World Aquarium. If you would otherwise buy waterpark tickets for every day (compare them in our Dubai water parks guide), the room price looks very different.

For younger children there is a separate water playground and a fully supervised kids' club with a daily programme; Wavehouse adds bowling, a wave machine and a play area. With 16 restaurants, from Shawafel and DXB Burger to Nobu and Hakkasan, you never have to leave the island.

Compared with Jumeirah Beach Hotel (#4, €471), you pay €90 less for a larger waterpark and a bigger resort, but give up Jumeirah Beach Hotel's location score (9.5) and its kids' club access written into every rate. Compared with Le Meridien (#2, €235), you pay €146 more for the bigger park, the aquarium and a higher score (9.2 vs 8.5).

The catches: there are no extra beds (cots for 0–3 are free), so a family of four may need two rooms or a suite; the room price excludes the service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the tourism fee; and selected areas are under enhancement work.

review: Le Meridien Mina Seyahi is the cheapest way on this page to get a beach, a kids' club and an included waterpark in one booking. At €235 a night the Deluxe Skyline View room comes with unlimited access to Jungle Bay waterpark (slides, a wave pool and more), named in the room description.

For children there is the Le Meridien Family Kids Club with activity programmes and beach games, two separate kids' pools, and a 1,200-metre beach with a water sports centre. It also prices the same room for three guests (€297) and four (€359), which makes the family maths easy.
Against Atlantis (#1) you save €146 a night but get a smaller waterpark and no aquarium. Against Jumeirah Beach Hotel (#4) you save €236, but its rate also includes kids' club access and Wild Wadi.

The catches: the cheapest room is only 32 m², breakfast is not listed on the €235 rate (the cheapest breakfast rate is €275, and breakfast is €33 on the three- and four-guest room-only rates), and taxes come on top. Barasti Bar on the beach has live entertainment in the evening.

review: Lapita is the Dubai Parks hotel to book if you want resort comfort, not just a bed. review: Jumeirah Beach Hotel is the most expensive resort on this page at €471 a night, and the reason is in the room name: kids' club access and daily Wild Wadi Water Park entry are included on every room type listed, from the Ocean View Deluxe up.

It also has the best address for a beach holiday: a private beach area, Jumeira Public Beach a six-minute walk, and the page's highest location score (9.5). Four pools include a kids' pool with a shallow end, and seven restaurants and bars (Fika, Dhow and Anchor, Aila's Table, Nuska Beach) keep dinner on site.

For a family of four, the Ocean View Family Deluxe Room with Murphy wall beds (two singles plus an extra-large double) shows €545 with breakfast for two adults; add the children to the search to see the family price. Compared with Atlantis (#1), you pay €90 more for a smaller waterpark, but get the page's best location score (9.5) and kids' club access in every rate.

The catches: extra beds cost AED 200 per child a night, a 10% service charge, taxes and an AED 20 tourism fee come on top, and the free-cancellation window closes on 23 December for mid-January dates.

review: Grand Hyatt Dubai is the family pick for a city base. At €286 a night you get a 39 m² room in a 710-room resort with its own waterpark, 15 minutes by car from Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall. That makes it easy to mix pool days with sightseeing.

The resort side is real: an outdoor pool area, an indoor pool, a tropical atrium garden and 11 restaurants (Awtar, Andiamo!, Peppercrab, iZ, Wox). Connecting Grand rooms can be requested for families who need two rooms side by side.

Read the rate carefully: waterpark access is included on eligible rate plans, not every one. Compared with Le Meridien (#2), you pay €51 more, lose the beach and the guaranteed waterpark, but gain a much shorter ride to Downtown.
The catches: no beach, children 12+ pay as adults, extra beds are AED 150 a night, and an AED 1,000 cash deposit is collected at check-in.

review: Al Jaddaf Rotana is not a resort, and that is the point. For €167 a night (a deal rate on our date), less than any beach resort room here, you get an 80 m² One Bedroom Suite with a separate bedroom, living room, two bathrooms, a full kitchen and a washing machine. For bigger families, Two Bedroom Suites start at €248.
It also has the friendliest extra-bed rules on the page: cots and extra beds are free for children under 3, and extra beds cost AED 100 a night after that. The guest score is 9.2, with staff at 9.5.

Use it as a base: Al Jaddaf Metro is a 5-minute walk, and Downtown, Dubai Mall and Dubai Frame are close. Spend the days at a waterpark or on a family desert safari, and come back to a kitchen and separate bedrooms. Compared with Grand Hyatt (#6), you get twice the space for €119 less, but no waterpark.
The catches: one pool, no kids' club, no beach, and breakfast is €30 extra on some suite rates.

guide.h2: Dubai Family Resorts Compared: Price, Kids' Club, Waterpark and Extra Beds
guide.html:
All ten prices are the lowest nightly rate for two adults on the same January weeknight, before service charges and taxes (for LEGOLAND Hotel, the cheapest room that sleeps a family). Rates marked * were limited-time deal rates that night. The column that changes the picture is what is included: three resorts put a waterpark in every room rate (Atlantis, Le Meridien, Jumeirah Beach Hotel), and three Dubai Parks hotels sell rooms with theme-park access. The second column to read is extra beds: Atlantis, Rove, Centara and LEGOLAND Hotel have none, so a family of four needs a family room, a bunk-bed room or two rooms.

Family of four: what one room really costs

Because the headline prices are for two adults, here are the rates the resorts themselves sell for bigger groups in one room:

  • Le Meridien Mina Seyahi: the same Deluxe room priced for four guests at €359 (room only) or €399 with breakfast, Jungle Bay included.
  • Lapita: two-double room for four from €297 with breakfast and free cancellation, theme-park access included.
  • Rove At The Park: 46 m² Family Interconnecting room with Dubai Parks tickets, €358 (up to three on the rate shown).
  • Jumeirah Beach Hotel: Ocean View Family Deluxe with two Murphy wall beds from €545 with breakfast for two adults; children's extra beds are AED 200 a night.
  • Al Jaddaf Rotana: Two Bedroom Suite from €248 (a deal rate, shown for two adults), with free extra beds for under-3s.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Family Resort Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Best all-round, waterpark included: #1 Atlantis, The Palm, €381. Daily Aquaventure and aquarium access, a supervised kids' club and 16 restaurants.
  • Waterpark and beach for less: #2 Le Meridien Mina Seyahi, €235, with unlimited Jungle Bay and a four-person rate at €359.
  • LEGOLAND and MOTIONGATE days: #3 Lapita, €235 for a 5★ pool resort, #8 Rove At The Park, €76 on a budget, or #10 LEGOLAND Hotel, €248 for a themed bunk-bed room with park access and breakfast.
  • Beachfront with kids' club and waterpark in every rate: #4 Jumeirah Beach Hotel, €471.
  • Toddlers and younger kids on the beach: #5 Hilton Dubai Palm Jumeirah, €254, with the Pirate's Kids Club and a shaded kids' pool.
  • Sightseeing plus a waterpark: #6 Grand Hyatt, €286, 15 minutes from Burj Khalifa.
  • Space and a kitchen: #7 Al Jaddaf Rotana, €167, for an 80 m² suite by the metro.
  • Breakfast and dinner in the price: #9 Centara Mirage, €238, family room with two double beds.

Splitting the stay? Many families do a few nights at Dubai Parks for the theme parks and the rest by the sea. For beachfront options without the kids' focus, see our JBR hotels comparison and Palm Jumeirah hotels.

guide.h2: Planning a Family Stay in Dubai: Areas, Getting Around and Extra Costs
guide.html:
Which area suits which family

  • Palm Jumeirah (Atlantis, Hilton): location scores 9.3–9.4, private beaches, and Aquaventure on the Palm itself. Mall of the Emirates is about 20 minutes and Burj Khalifa 25 minutes from Atlantis by car.
  • Jumeirah and Al Sufouh beaches (Jumeirah Beach Hotel, Le Meridien): beach resorts with waterpark access in the room rate (Wild Wadi and Jungle Bay). Jumeirah Beach Hotel scores 9.5 for location.
  • Dubai Parks and Resorts (Lapita, Rove, LEGOLAND Hotel): walk to LEGOLAND, LEGOLAND Water Park, MOTIONGATE and Real Madrid World, but you are out of town (Al Maktoum International is 19 km away). Location scores are 7.9–8.7.
  • City (Grand Hyatt, Al Jaddaf Rotana): no beach, but 15 minutes or a short metro ride from Downtown and Dubai Mall.
  • Dubai Islands (Centara Mirage): beach resort 11 km from Dubai International Airport.

Getting around

Al Jaddaf Rotana is the only pick with a metro station on foot (5 minutes to Al Jaddaf). Lapita includes a shuttle to Mall of the Emirates and Dubai Mall and beach access at Sheraton JBR. Everywhere else, plan on taxis or a car: parking is free at most of the ten.

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: the nightly prices above exclude them. Where the rates break them down, a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and a Dubai tourism fee of AED 10–20 per room per night are added on top.
  • Extra beds: AED 100 (Al Jaddaf Rotana), 125 (Le Meridien), 150 (Lapita, Hilton Palm, Grand Hyatt) or 200 (Jumeirah Beach Hotel) a night. Atlantis, Rove, Centara and LEGOLAND Hotel have none. Cots are free everywhere they are offered.
  • When kids pay as adults: from 12 at Grand Hyatt, from 18 at Le Meridien, Hilton Palm and Al Jaddaf Rotana.
  • Cash deposits: AED 1,000 at Grand Hyatt and AED 500 at Centara, refunded at check-out.
  • Breakfast: €30 (Al Jaddaf Rotana), €33 (Le Meridien), about €29 more at Hilton Palm; included in Centara's half board, LEGOLAND's €248 themed rate and Rove's €213 ticket rate.
  • Waterpark and park tickets: included at Atlantis, Le Meridien and Jumeirah Beach Hotel; on eligible rates at Grand Hyatt; in Lapita's room rate; in LEGOLAND Hotel's themed rate and on Rove's ticket rates. Centara has an on-site waterpark, but its rates do not say whether entry is included. Elsewhere, compare water park tickets before you go.

When to go

The rates here are for mid-January, in the cooler winter months. For an evening away from the resort, compare Dubai dinner cruises.

faqs.q: What is the best family resort in Dubai?
faqs.a: Atlantis, The Palm, from €381 a night for two adults. It includes daily Aquaventure World and Lost World Aquarium access, a supervised kids' club and 16 restaurants, with a 9.2 guest score. For a cheaper waterpark resort, Le Meridien Mina Seyahi (€235) includes unlimited Jungle Bay access and has a kids' club and beach.

faqs.q: Which Dubai hotels include waterpark access?
faqs.a: Atlantis, The Palm (Aquaventure, daily), Jumeirah Beach Hotel (Wild Wadi, daily, plus kids' club access) and Le Meridien Mina Seyahi (unlimited Jungle Bay) include it in the room rate. Grand Hyatt Dubai includes its own waterpark on eligible rate plans, and LEGOLAND Hotel's themed rates include park access.

faqs.q: Which Dubai hotel is best for LEGOLAND and MOTIONGATE?
faqs.a: Lapita (€235) is a short walk from LEGOLAND, LEGOLAND Water Park, MOTIONGATE and Real Madrid World, with theme-park access in the room rate, a kids' club and four-guest rooms from €297 with breakfast. On a budget, Rove At The Park starts at €76; for themed bunk-bed rooms, LEGOLAND Hotel starts at €248 with park access and breakfast. See our theme parks comparison to choose the park.

faqs.q: Can a family of four stay in one room in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, at some resorts. Le Meridien Mina Seyahi prices its Deluxe room for four at €359, Lapita sells two-double rooms for four from €297 with breakfast, and Jumeirah Beach Hotel has a Family Deluxe Room with Murphy wall beds. Atlantis, Rove, Centara and LEGOLAND Hotel have no extra beds, so check the room's occupancy before booking.

faqs.q: Do children stay free in Dubai hotels?
faqs.a: Cots for babies (usually 0–2, 0–3 at Atlantis, Hilton Palm and Grand Hyatt) are free wherever a price is listed. Extra beds cost AED 100–200 a night, except at Al Jaddaf Rotana, where they are free for under-3s. Children are charged as adults from 12 at Grand Hyatt and from 18 at Le Meridien, Hilton Palm and Al Jaddaf Rotana.

faqs.q: How much does a family resort in Dubai cost per night?
faqs.a: For two adults on a January weeknight, the ten options here ran from €76 (Rove At The Park) to €471 (Jumeirah Beach Hotel), with beach resorts with a kids' club mostly at €235–381. A service charge (usually 10%), VAT, a municipality fee and a tourism fee of AED 10–20 per room per night come on top, plus extra beds for children.

faqs.q: Which Dubai hotel has the best kids' club on the beach?
faqs.a: For younger children, Hilton Dubai Palm Jumeirah's Pirate's Kids Club (toys, films, sandcastles, shaded kids' pool) at €254 a night, with a 9.0 score. Atlantis has a fully supervised daily programme, Le Meridien adds beach games and two kids' pools, and Jumeirah Beach Hotel includes kids' club access in every room rate.

methodology: We compared more than 20 Dubai family resorts and hotels on live prices for the same night (two adults, one night in mid-January) and kept the 10 that give a genuinely different choice for families: waterpark resorts, beach resorts with kids' clubs, theme-park hotels at Dubai Parks and a city suite hotel, from €76 to €471. Each was scored on the nightly price, guest and location score, kids' club, whether waterpark or theme-park access is included, family room size and who it sleeps, child and extra-bed policies, beach and pools, and breakfast cost. Rankings reward the best all-round family stay first, then the clearest pick for each type of family.
